target.title: fix: stop selected channel sessions from WebChat
target.body:
Supersedes #101495

Related: #91987

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users viewing a running channel session in Control UI could not stop it with `/stop` or the stop action when that run was started outside the browser. The selected session appeared active, but the browser had no local run ID, so the stop request did not reach that channel session.

## Why This Change Was Made

Browser-owned runs still use the existing run-ID-targeted `chat.abort` path. When no browser-local run ID exists, Control UI now sends `sessions.abort` for the exact selected session. After agent/session resolution and existing authorization, the Gateway clears that non-global session's queued successors and aborts its exact persisted embedded/reply run before signaling tracked runs, preventing a draining run from starting queued work.

This rebuild is intentionally narrower than #101495: it does not scan hidden controllers or pending registries, does not widen `chat.abort` authorization, and does not fabricate a run ID for reply-only work. Foreign connection-owned chat runs and worker runs remain untouched. Canonical global scope stays on its existing `chat.abort` behavior because the shared literal `global` queue has no safe per-agent cleanup identity; this PR targets distinct channel sessions.

## User Impact

Control UI users can stop the exact selected Weixin, Telegram, or other channel session even when that work was started by the channel rather than the current browser. Other channel sessions continue running, queued work for the selected session cannot restart after the stop, and browser-owned run cancellation keeps its existing targeted behavior.

## Evidence

Current-head automated proof:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/chat.abort-authorization.test.ts` — 19 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.abort-agent-scope.test.ts` — 28 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.test.ts -- -t handleAbortChat` — 15 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/e2e/chat-flow.e2e.test.ts -- -t "sends /stop to the exact selected channel session"` — 1 passed
- Core production, core test, and UI `tsgo` lanes passed.
- Targeted `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed for all eight changed files.
- Fresh branch autoreview completed with no accepted/actionable findings (correctness 0.93).
- GitHub Actions CI run [29668732613](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29668732613) completed with the aggregate gate and all selected code, UI, type, lint, build, QA smoke, security, and dependency checks passing.

Current-head runtime proof on `75616c9423eab41340c7ebd89414fe7d15c5f0d4` used a temporary uncommitted QA Lab scenario with a real Gateway child, three qa-channel accounts, the mock OpenAI provider, and the real browser Control UI. The scenario passed both steps and proved:

- Control UI submitted exactly `sessions.abort` for the selected channel session, with no `chat.abort` or `chat.send` submission.
- The selected session changed from `hasActiveRun: true` to `false`.
- A second channel session remained `hasActiveRun: true`.
- The queued selected-session successor produced zero model requests and zero outbound messages after the stop.

The Mantis Telegram workflow run [29668945795](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29668945795) did not capture comparable video because its target session had already reached `done` when the stop RPC arrived; it is not used as current-head proof. Prior #101495 recordings are retained only as scenario context:

- [Selected channel session stops](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/25f32135-1f1a-4f9c-b0a7-ddade5464b86)
- [Other channel sessions remain active](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e5b78d13-90c5-416f-a354-610fef9b6c59)

target.title: fix(extensions): bound extension source read with size cap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `extensionSourceNeedsJitiAliasResolution` function reads entire extension source files into memory with no size bound. Extension source files can be large (compiled bundles, bundled dependencies), risking OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

The function used raw `fs.readFileSync(extensionPath, "utf8")` with no size bound, risking OOM on large files. The fix uses the internal `readRegularFileSync` wrapper (via `infra/regular-file.ts`) with a 10 MiB cap:

1. Rejects symlinks and non-regular files (returns `true`, sending to jiti)
2. Caps reads at 10 MiB — larger files return `true` for jiti fallback
3. Returns the bounded content for source inspection

## User Impact

- Prevents OOM crashes when scanning large extension source files
- Oversized extensions are still loaded (via jiti) — no functionality lost

## Evidence

**`pnpm test src/agents/sessions/extensions/loader.native-js.test.ts`** — all 11 tests pass, including the new oversized extension fallback test:
```
 ✓ |agents| src/agents/sessions/extensions/loader.native-js.test.ts (11 tests)
     ✓ falls back to jiti for oversized extension source files  458ms
     ...
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  11 passed (11)
```

target.title: fix(telegram): preserve per-image captions in media group albums (#110690)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a user sends multiple images as a Telegram media group (album), each
image can carry its own caption. `processMediaGroup` aggregates the group
into a single agent turn but selects only one "primary" message —
`entry.messages.find(m => m.msg.caption || m.msg.text)`. The aggregated
turn's text comes from this single primary; every other per-image caption
is silently dropped, so the agent never sees them.

Additionally, the original fix numbered captions by their position within
the _captioned_ subset (`i + 1` over `perImageCaptions`) rather than by
their 1-based album position. When images 1 and 3 have captions but image 2
does not, the agent would see them labeled `Image 1` / `Image 2` instead of
the correct `Image 1` / `Image 3`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before dispatching the primary message to `processMessageWithReplyChain`,
collect every non-empty caption from all messages in the group and combine
them into a labeled list (`Image 1: caption\nImage 2: caption\n...`). When
multiple captions exist, the combined text replaces the primary message's
`caption` field so the downstream `resolveTelegramTextContent` (which
prefers `msg.text` over `msg.caption`) can surface all captions to the agent.

The caption collection is extracted into an exported `collectMediaGroupCaptions`
helper so sparse-caption indexing can be tested in isolation.

## User Impact

Albums where each image has a distinct caption — e.g. "before"/"after"
comparisons, per-dish food logs, labeled screenshots — now deliver every
caption to the agent instead of only the first one.

## Evidence

### Root cause trace

```
processMediaGroup
  → primary = first message with caption/text  ← only ONE caption preserved
  → processMessageWithReplyChain(primary.msg, allMedia)
    → resolveTelegramTextContent(msg.text, msg.caption)  ← reads caption from primary only
  ✗ Other images' caption fields never collected
```

### Behavior

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 3 images, each with caption | Only Image 1's caption sent | `Image 1: ca\nImage 2: cb\nImage 3: cc` |
| 3 images, only 1st and 3rd captioned | Only Image 1's caption sent | `Image 1: ca\nImage 3: cc` |
| 1 image with caption | No change | No change |
| No captions | No change | No change |

### Tests

```
npx vitest run extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.inbound-media-group.runtime.test.ts
```

8 tests covering:
- Empty / no-caption messages → `[]`
- Single caption → single entry
- All captioned → preserves album indexes 1..N
- Sparse captions → retains original album position (not subset index)
- Whitespace / empty string filtering
- Trim behavior
- Large sparse group (10 messages, every 3rd captioned)

### Not tested

- Live Telegram media group roundtrip (requires Telegram bot token and
  real chat). The fix is a mechanical collection pass before the
  existing dispatch call; the code path is shared with the existing
  single-caption path.

## Files changed

| File | Changes |
|---|---|
| `extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.inbound-media-group.runtime.ts` | Extract `collectMediaGroupCaptions` helper with album-index tracking; use it in `processMediaGroup`; `messages[i]?.caption?.trim()` for `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` compliance |
| `extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.inbound-media-group.runtime.test.ts` | +8 tests: sparse-caption coverage for `collectMediaGroupCaptions` |
